objective:
the automation page hands the detail pane back on any click, and a landed decision refetches its own desk

Selecting a bot, a desk or a wall section while the automation page was open
changed a selection nobody could see: the page owns the whole detail pane, so
the room read as frozen until you found its close button. select() now closes
it. Merely opening the page still decides nothing about what is underneath.

A GitHub decision that applied now refetches that one desk before answering,
about two GraphQL points, so the app refresh that already follows decide() sees
the closed issue gone instead of waiting out the next minute build. A decision
that failed changed nothing on GitHub and a runtime kind never asked it
anything, so neither spends a refresh.

The refetch can never unsay the decision. It reaches GitHub again on its own,
past the one guard refresh_desk has, so a timeout or a throwing rate reader
would have turned an already-closed issue into a 500, and what a person does
with a button that failed is press it again. It is wrapped, the failure is
logged honestly, and the answer stays the one the decision earned.

All three regressions fail on the old code first: three XCTAssertFalse on
automationOpen, the desk list empty where it should hold one repo, and 500
where the close still stands.
